rounds.fact: Suck.com pioneered a sarcastic, link-heavy, first-person writing style that influenced blog voice for years, despite the site itself shutting down back in 2001.
Nintendo's site in the early 2000s was promoting both the GameCube and Game Boy Advance simultaneously, an unusually broad two-console push even by Nintendo's standards.
Epicurious launched in 1995 as one of the first major recipe websites, built from the archives of Condé Nast's food magazines like Gourmet and Bon Appétit.
Salon launched in 1995 as one of the first online-only magazines with no print edition at all, betting entirely on the web as a legitimate home for serious journalism.
PayPal originally grew by paying users real money just to sign up and refer friends, an aggressive growth tactic that helped it become the dominant way to pay on eBay.
